correctness.rationale: With fixed positive receiving and source strengths, the characteristic polynomial depends on layout only through the reciprocal kernel product; the Perron root is strictly increasing in this product. Independently expanding the wrapped geometric moments, with x=q/(1-q) and τ=z(1-z), gives the spacing-dependent parts of (1-q)^2 P_{k-1}(z)P_{k-1}(1-z) as 0, τ, τ², and τ³−3x(1+x)τ², respectively. In the last case the derivative changes from negative to positive at 2x(1+x) when that point lies below 1/4. The endpoint difference is proportional to 1−14q+q² and the interior-minimum condition to 1−10q+q²>0, yielding the two stated, distinct roots. At the global tie the central and coincident maxima are the only maximizers on the closure, and the minimum has τ=1/6; at the minimum merger the antipode is the unique minimum. On the distinct-site domain the coincidence-only regime has an unattained supremum, not an interior optimum. The exact q=1/2, z=1/10 witness gives the stated positive excess 19469/15625 over the antipode. Stage-one spectral invariance is for distinct sites only; the diagonal convention at the directional jump is held fixed.
residual_risks: No implication for finite-width sites, unequal stage rates, more sites, stages k≥5 or field-measured recruitment.

value.rationale: The natural point-site extension of the exponential and two-stage laws has a genuinely different optimum, with the first stage count allowing reversal proved and a strict distinct-site witness. Separating the global endpoint tie from the interior-minimum merger answers a useful qualitative question that a spacing comparison at only one rate or two fixed layouts would miss.
residual_risks: This is a model-level parameter boundary, not a conservation prescription or claim about measured dispersal.
